Overview
--------

Onslaught is one of the gamemodes in Dungeon Defenders 2, which features stronger [enemies](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Enemies "Enemies")
 as you progress.  
Onslaught is available as soon as you complete the [Campaign](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Campaign "Campaign")
. You'll start on floor 1, begining your journey to floor 999!

### Features

Onslaught has many special features that aren't present in other gamemodes. Here is a list of the special features:

*   The further you progress through floors in Onslaught, the higher level [enemies](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Enemies "Enemies")
     will become.  
    

The [enemy](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Enemies "Enemies")
 level scaling of onslaught is rather low at 172.5 levels per floor (floor 36-945).  

After completing floor 945 the scaling starts to go up exponentially at 402,500 levels per floor (floor 946-999).  

Shortly into the exponential scaling, all [enemies'](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Enemies "Enemies")
 health gradually reaches the [32bit Interger limit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/32-bit_computing)
 and decides to cap at a flat 2 billion HP.

  

*   Every lane has special conditions as to which [monsters](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Enemies "Enemies")
     can spawn from it. The name of the lane will also change as well to indicate what will spawn there.  
    

Lanes will have set prefixes, suffixes, or names that will appear on a lane and determine what spawns from it. e.g. **Cy =** [cyborks](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Cybork "Cybork")
, **Frost =** [Frost Enemies](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Frost_Enemies "Frost Enemies")
.

**Main Article:** **[Onslaught Lane Schedules](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Onslaught_Lane_Schedules "Onslaught Lane Schedules")
**

  

*   [Enemies](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Enemies "Enemies")
     can be affected by [lane mutators](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Mutators "Mutators")
    . You will probably encounter your first [lane mutator](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Mutators "Mutators")
     at floor 3.

[Lane mutators](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Mutators "Mutators")
 can be viewed by [holding shift](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Controls "Controls")
 and will appear below the list of [enemies](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Enemies "Enemies")
. The further you go in Onslaught, the more [mutators](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Mutators "Mutators")
 that will appear in each game.

Each lane is limited to 2 [mutators](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Mutators "Mutators")
 at a time, [double mutators](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Mutators "Mutators")
 start at floor 22. Re-rolling an onslaught floor will re-roll the [mutators](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Mutators "Mutators")
, lanes and [map](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Maps "Maps")
.

**Main Article:** **[Mutators](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Mutators "Mutators")
**

  

*   Each floor has a [map](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Maps "Maps")
     pool (listed below) and a forced [map](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Maps "Maps")
    , [The Lost Temple](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/The_Lost_Temple "The Lost Temple")
     that every player needs to do when pushing their onslaught floors. Temple will occur every 10 floors starting from 34 and has unique mechanics to overcome.  
    

**Main Article:** **[The Lost Temple](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/The_Lost_Temple "The Lost Temple")
**

Chaos Level
-----------

Each floor has a difficulty associated with it that determines what [chaos](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Chaos "Chaos")
 [enemies](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Enemies "Enemies")
 can spawn, as well as what kinds of rewards can drop in terms of equipment, [shards](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Shards "Shards")
, [crafting materials](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Crafting_Materials "Crafting Materials")
, and [mods](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Mods "Mods")
.  
**Note:** Completing an [expedition](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Expeditions "Expeditions")
 will automatically set your floor to the minimum floor in it's range. This does not apply to [Chaos 10 expeditions](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Expeditions "Expeditions")
.  
In order to access a specific chaos tier to skip some Onslaught floors through [expeditions](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Expeditions "Expeditions")
, a minimum [champion score](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Champion_Score "Champion Score")
 must be met.

| Chaos Level | Floor Equivalent | Floor Unlock | Champion Score |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Campaign | 1~2 | 1   | 0   |
| Chaos 1 | 3~4 | 3   | 335 |
| Chaos 2 | 5~8 | 5   | 580 |
| Chaos 3 | 9~11 | 9   | 1,050 |
| Chaos 4 | 12~16 | 12  | 1,740 |
| Chaos 5 | 17~21 | 17  | 2,750 |
| Chaos 6 | 22~27 | 22  | 3,800 |
| Chaos 7 | 28~98 | 28  | 5,300 |
| Chaos 8 | 99~299 | 99  | 7,850 |
| Chaos 9 | 300~699 | 300 | 9,850 |
| Chaos 10 | 700~999 | N/A | 12,750 |

Map Pools
---------

Onslaught has a [map](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Maps "Maps")
 pool system per floor. Each floor's pool can be identified with the last digit of the floor number.  
e.g. floor 105 will be one of the [maps](https://wiki.dungeondefenders2.com/wiki/Maps "Maps")
 in it's category below.  
The last digit rule applies floor 33+, groups stay the same always but before then the last digit rule doesn't work.
